features.description: Authenticate MCP clients and isolate user, agent, client, and downstream session state outside model-controlled arguments.
acceptanceCriteria: Untrusted arguments cannot select or override identity.
Credentials are audience-bound, route-scoped, short-lived where possible, and never returned to the agent.
Sessions cannot observe or mutate another session's routes, state, approvals, quotas, results, or audit context.
Identity rotation quarantines trust and invalidates incompatible active state.

progress.completionEvidence: The authenticated HTTP boundary resolves identity before MCP parsing and binds it to an opaque session. A disposable gateway credential vault verifies credential digests and issues metadata-only leases capped at five minutes and bound to one profile revision, audience, route, session, and namespace. An authenticated compartment repository isolates routes, downstream state, approvals, quotas, results, and audit entries; cross-session access fails without revealing existence. Same-subject credential or identity-revision rotation quarantines the session, freezes shadow trust, clears active routes/state/approvals/quotas, retains results/audit for accountability, revokes session leases, and rejects both old and rotated identities. Evidence uses disposable in-memory repositories and TEST_FIXTURE authentication only.

features.description: Defend the MCP protocol against replay, flooding, recursion, oversized payloads, runaway concurrency, timeouts, and dependency failure.

Quotas cover user, agent, client, session, server, tool, route, destination, and action family.
Call depth, delegation depth, fan-out, payload size, result size, concurrency, redirects, retries, and execution time are bounded.
Recursive or cyclic calls are detected and stopped.
Cancellation, circuit breakers, and dependency failures leave protected mutations denied and audited.

completedCriteria: Timestamps, nonces, request IDs, bounded clock skew, and replay caches reject replayed traffic.

progress.completionEvidence: A disposable host-neutral protocol guard validates versioned operation requests, enforces bounded timestamp skew, and keeps request-ID and nonce replay caches scoped by authenticated session. Admission and runtime checkpoints enforce payload, expected/observed result, depth, delegation, fan-out, redirect, retry, and deadline limits; equivalent ancestor route/destination/action signatures detect recursion. PostgreSQL administration requires an authenticated principal plus explicit authorization and appends immutable versioned SERVER, ROUTE, SCHEMA, and POLICY documents and audit events. All eleven required analyzer categories fail unknown or substituted analysis safely. The approved HashiCorp Vault KV v2 adapter permits HTTPS except for an explicit disposable-loopback mode, retrieves one exact version at use time, rejects revision/reference/origin/redirect substitution, bounds responses, and zeroizes its token buffers. A real checksum-verified Vault 1.21.1 dev server was exercised on loopback: revision 1 was retrieved through the non-exporting broker and supplied only to one exact session/audience/route/origin-bound disposable downstream request. Dev-mode evidence completes the provider implementation criterion but does not establish production credential custody or production coverage.

features.description: Validate the operational runtime with named MCP hosts, adaptive repeated trials, and independently reviewed evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: At least two named independently operated MCP hosts complete benign and adversarial workflows through the runtime.
Adaptive repeated trials retain complete trajectory metrics, baselines, configuration digests, and reproducible evidence.
An independent security review records findings, remediation, and authorized residual-risk disposition.

progress.completionEvidence: Safe preparation now includes strict named-host, paired operational-trial, and independent-security-review evidence contracts. The review contract binds reviewer independence declarations, exact source/runtime/configuration digests, findings, remediation, and separately authorized residual risk; it rejects reviewer self-authorization, inconsistent dispositions, missing remediation evidence, and digest substitution. These contracts remain EVIDENCE_CONTRACT_ONLY and do not satisfy any acceptance criterion without two real independently operated hosts, actual repeated operational trajectories, and a genuinely independent review.

features.description: Produce a production-candidate deployment with exclusive-mediation evidence, signed artifacts, and exercised recovery.
acceptanceCriteria: Independent network, IAM, sandbox, operating-system, and downstream controls prove direct and alternate protected paths blocked.
Production-scoped coverage probes establish fresh exact-scope evidence before protected mutations are enabled.
Artifacts and SBOM are reproducible, signed, verified, dependency-audited, and tied to an exact source revision.
Upgrade, incident response, recovery, and rollback procedures have named owners, objectives, and retained exercise evidence.

features.description: Implement a functional authenticated human approval and audit web interface connected to the protected runtime.
acceptanceCriteria: A runnable browser UI loads live pending approvals and canonical context from the protected gateway; no approval, outcome, or coverage field is supplied by static mock data or model-authored summaries.

The approval transport authenticates the human independently, authorizes the exact policy scope, protects session and request integrity, rejects cross-user access, CSRF, origin confusion, stale state, and client-supplied decision authority, and exposes no credential or approval secret.
The interface offers only exact Approve once and Deny actions, displays expiry and current status, and contains no bulk, persistent, wildcard, or always-allow control.

Approval, denial, expiry, revocation, reload, duplicate click, multi-tab race, reconnect, and concurrent consumption produce one durable PostgreSQL state transition and at most one exact downstream forwarding attempt.

The browser displays the governed outcome, recovery class, related attempts, truthful coverage, and exact missing guarantees from correlated durable records, with accessible keyboard operation and unambiguous confirmation/error states.

Automated browser and integration tests exercise a real pending request through authenticated human decision, PostgreSQL consumption, exact forwarding, governed result, audit display, and all fail-closed negative paths before the feature is complete.

progress.completionEvidence: Added the authenticated approval web boundary, strict digest-only session/CSRF/origin/ETag contracts, PostgreSQL persistence migration/store, and dependency-free accessible UI assets. Browser/server routes, session creation, CSRF header, and error contracts now agree; browser-style same-origin reads, origin confusion, identity rotation, system-attributed expiry, immutable approval binding, denial concurrency, and migration inventory are tested. Build, lint, typecheck, 32 unit files/288 tests, 14 integration files/61 tests, and all 21 feature records pass. The PostgreSQL store and web app still expose incompatible store interfaces, so protected runtime composition and end-to-end browser evidence remain outstanding.
